solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Criminal bosses' secret source of power to bypass an economic system

parts.note: capi is the Italian plural of capo, a Mafia boss

indicators.note: bypassing a word means going round it, leaving it out of what came before

parts.note: a talisman is a charm credited with hidden magical power
taken as written

explanation.surface: Mob bosses route their secret power past the official economy.
explanation.walkthrough: Capi is the Italian plural of capo, the Mafia title; a talisman is a charm thought to hold magic power. 'to bypass' means skip round the word 'an'.
explanation.definitionFit: Capitalism is the private-ownership economic order, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Dressed up in bridal clobber

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the run of letters is read from bottom to top
the letters sit inside the words bridal clobber, spanning the gap between them

explanation.surface: Someone decked out in wedding finery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' hides DALC across 'bridAL Clobber'; 'up' turns it round. 'Clobber' is British slang for clothes, which helps the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Clad is an old past participle of clothe, so it means wearing clothes.

clue.text: Report of whales stranded

parts.note: a pod is a group of whales
cast, as in cast ashore or castaway, means stranded

explanation.surface: A news item about a group of whales beached on the shore.
explanation.definitionFit: A podcast is a broadcast audio programme, which can serve as a news report.

clue.text: What'll make tune go wrong? It's hard to say

indicators.note: going wrong means the letters of tune go are jumbled into a different order

parts.note: a twister is something that twists, the thing that makes the letters go wrong

explanation.surface: A puzzle about mangling a melody, ending with a sigh that it is difficult to articulate.
explanation.walkthrough: TUNE GO rearranged gives TONGUE, and what does the twisting is a TWISTER, so the wordplay names itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A tongue twister is a phrase deliberately difficult to pronounce, so it is literally hard to say.

clue.text: Boost for Brussels Hibernian association

indicators.note: to boost is to raise, and in a down clue raising means the letters are read upwards

parts.note: Brussels, seat of its institutions, stands for the European Union, EU
Hibernia is Latin for Ireland, so a Hibernian is an Irish Gael

explanation.surface: Brussels funding helps an Irish society, or perhaps the Edinburgh football club Hibernian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boost' turns EU + GAEL upwards. Hibernian is also a Scottish football club, which suits the football sense of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A league is an alliance or union of people or groups, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Two legal items in baggage

parts.note: a suit is a legal action, the first of the two
a case is a legal action, the second of the two

explanation.surface: Two legal documents packed in someone's luggage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two legal items' gives two words, SUIT and CASE, each a lawsuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A suitcase is a piece of luggage, an example of baggage.

clue.text: Destroyer without a weapon

indicators.note: without means the following a is left out of the god's name

parts.note: Shiva is the Hindu god known as the Destroyer

explanation.surface: A warship that has no armament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Destroyer' looks like a warship, but it is the Hindu god Shiva; 'without a' removes his final A.
explanation.definitionFit: Shiv is slang for a knife, especially an improvised one, so a weapon.

clue.text: He'd got free with one bound

indicators.note: setting the letters free lets them be rearranged

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: An escape artist breaks loose in a single leap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound' looks like a leap, but it is the definition: tied up.
explanation.definitionFit: Hogtied means tied by all four limbs, so thoroughly bound.

clue.text: I, fired with a passion unconsummated, got over thy heartless inconstancy

indicators.note: in a down clue, getting over means the letters climb upwards, read in reverse

parts.note: lit means fired, set alight

indicators.note: unconsummated means not completed, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: love is a passion

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter of thy is cut out

explanation.surface: A jilted lover laments a fickle partner whose passion was never fulfilled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unconsummated' means love is left unfinished, losing its E; 'got over' turns the first four pieces upwards into VOLATILI. 'heartless' strips the H from the middle of thy.
explanation.definitionFit: Volatility is a tendency to change suddenly, the same idea as fickleness.

clue.text: Extras dead and gone

indicators.note: gone suggests the letters have gone haywire, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Film extras who have died and departed.
explanation.definitionFit: Addenda are things added to a book or document, so supplementary extras.

clue.text: Setter will knock back beer, knock out rector and get barred

parts.note: the setter refers to themselves as I, so setter will is I'll

indicators.note: knocking out a letter removes it from the word
knock back means turn backwards here, so beer's synonym is reversed

parts.note: lager is a type of beer

explanation.surface: A boozy setter downs a pint, flattens the vicar and is thrown out of the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knock back' reverses LAGER to REGAL; 'knock out rector' removes R, leaving EGAL. 'Knock back' looks like drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Barred means prohibited, the same sense as forbidden by law.

clue.text: Ragged chap who might be found in funny farm?

definitions.meaning: someone ragged is teased and ridiculed, an object of mockery

definitions.text: who might be found in funny farm?
definitions.meaning: on a farm that is literally funny the livestock would be cheerful animals

explanation.surface: A dishevelled man who might end up in a mental hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Funny farm' is slang for a psychiatric hospital; here it is read literally, a farm whose stock is amused.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who is made the target of general ridicule is someone ragged.

clue.text: Therapist involved in sharp practice?

parts.note: sharp practice usually means underhand dealing, but here it is a healing art done with needles

explanation.surface: A therapist mixed up in shady business dealings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sharp practice' means dishonest dealing; read literally it is a practice using sharp points.
explanation.definitionFit: This practitioner treats patients by inserting fine needles, literally sharp practice.

clue.text: Not altogether happy bathroom's done up in style that's supposed to be restful

indicators.note: in places the reversed piece inside the other

parts.words: style that's supposed to be restful
parts.note: ambient is a calm, atmospheric style of music meant to soothe

indicators.note: in a down clue, done up means turned upwards, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: lav, short for lavatory, is a bathroom; the 's is read as is

explanation.surface: Someone unhappy with a bathroom refitted in a supposedly calming style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'done up' reverses LAV to VAL, which goes 'in' AMBIENT. 'Done up' looks like redecoration.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambivalent means having mixed feelings, so only partly pleased.

clue.text: Dog incessantly fed will change shape

indicators.note: incessantly read as without ceasing, i.e. without its end, drops the last letter

parts.note: a mutt is a mongrel dog
ate means fed, took food

explanation.surface: A dog fed constantly will grow fat and change shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incessantly' is read as 'without its end', trimming MUTT to MUT.
explanation.definitionFit: To mutate is to undergo a change of form, transform.

clue.text: Snake holed up in plant

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake

indicators.note: up as in messed up, so the letters of holed are rearranged

explanation.surface: A snake hiding in a hole among the plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holed up' looks like hiding; 'up' is the anagram signal, turning HOLED into HODEL.
explanation.definitionFit: The asphodel is a lily-family flower, an example of a plant.

clue.text: Primates raised rebuke to create schism

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means lifted upwards, so the letters read backwards

parts.note: apes are primates
to rate is an old word for scold or rebuke

explanation.surface: Apes stand up and scold, splitting the troop.
explanation.walkthrough: RATE meaning scold is old-fashioned but still in dictionaries.
explanation.definitionFit: To separate is to split apart, which is what creating a schism does.

clue.text: Asks how paper might be selling

definitions.meaning: paper is sold ..., bundles of 24 or 25 sheets

explanation.surface: A shopper asks how a newspaper is selling.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as IN QUIRES: paper is sold by the quire, a bundle of sheets.
explanation.definitionFit: To ask is to put a question, the same as making an enquiry.

clue.text: Displaying apprehension in the capacity of ruler

parts.note: qua is Latin for in the capacity of, as
a king is a ruler

explanation.surface: A nervous monarch acting in an official role.
explanation.definitionFit: Trembling with fear shows apprehension, so this is fear made visible.

clue.text: Eat up — it's not serious, I hear

indicators.note: I hear signals the words are judged by how they sound

parts.note: something said in jest is not meant seriously

explanation.surface: Someone told to finish their food is assured it is only a joke.
explanation.definitionFit: To ingest is to take food into the body, to consume it.

clue.text: Jacob's daughter perhaps snaring man from the south in tangled web

indicators.note: snaring means catching and holding one piece inside the other
tangled means the letters of web are jumbled

parts.note: the word web is the fodder

indicators.note: in a down clue, from the south means reading upwards, backwards

parts.note: a male is a man

explanation.surface: A Biblical daughter trapping a man in a web.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jacob' suggests the Bible, but the Jacob is a breed of sheep. 'tangled' makes EWB from WEB; 'from the south' reverses MALE to ELAM, which the web is 'snaring'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jacob sheep's daughter would be a young female lamb, so an example of the answer.

clue.text: Woman introducing social network to another

indicators.note: introducing one piece to another puts it inside

parts.note: Edna is another woman's name
the WI, the Women's Institute, is a British social network of women's groups

explanation.surface: A woman introduces a friend to a social-media site.
explanation.walkthrough: The Women's Institute (WI) is a large British community organisation for women. 'social network' suggests the internet.
explanation.definitionFit: Edwina is a female given name, so an example of a woman.

clue.text: Early adopter tried satnav, losing way around outskirts of Geneva

indicators.note: a satnav losing its way goes round in a muddle, so the letters are rearranged
outskirts are the outer edges, so take the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A tech pioneer tries satellite navigation and gets lost on the edge of Geneva.
explanation.walkthrough: TRIED SATNAV plus GA, the edges of Geneva, are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: An avant-gardist is an innovator, someone among the first to take up new ideas.

clue.text: Internet phenomenon reinforced ego?

indicators.note: reinforced means doubled, so the piece is given twice

parts.note: the ego is the self, me

explanation.surface: An online craze that boosts someone's self-esteem.
explanation.definitionFit: A meme is an idea or image spread widely online, a viral phenomenon.

clue.text: I tear around following Queen and country

indicators.note: following means this piece comes after the Queen

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

indicators.note: around means the letters of i tear are moved around

explanation.surface: Someone rushes about after the monarch and the nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Eritrea is a nation in the Horn of Africa, an example of a country.

clue.text: Press silver badge at end of metalwork period

parts.note: to iron is to press clothes
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

indicators.note: at end means take the final letter of badge

explanation.surface: Instructions for pressing a silver badge at the end of a metalwork class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'metalwork period' sounds like a school lesson, but it is a prehistoric era.
explanation.definitionFit: This prehistoric era is named for the working of iron, so a period defined by metalwork.

clue.text: Follows men's cycling

indicators.note: cycling moves a letter round from one end of the word to the other

parts.note: stag means men-only, as in a stag night

explanation.surface: Following a men's cycling race.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of STAG cycles to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To tag along is to follow, and tags here means trails after someone.

clue.text: Homework that's been submitted again is so amazing

definitions.meaning: work handed in a second time can be marked once more

explanation.surface: A pupil's resubmitted homework turns out to be astonishing.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense splits the answer as RE-MARKABLE, able to be marked again.
explanation.definitionFit: Remarkable means worthy of note, extraordinary, very close to astonishing.
